sections.h2: What are your options for a quick sale in Lake Worth Beach?
sections.html:
Owners here can sell for cash, hire an agent or handle the sale alone. The cash route finishes sooner because no mortgage underwriting stands between contract and closing.

Hurricane season shapes ownership in this city, and the city's resident page points to evacuation zones, outage reporting and hurricane preparation. A tired roof or storm damage can stall a financed sale, while a direct buyer simply accounts for the repair in the price.

  • Cash buyer: repairs and showings fall away, and you pick the closing day.
  • Agent: more exposure, more steps.
  • Private sale: you draft and manage the paperwork with a title company.

The city names six historic districts: College Park, Old Lucerne, Old Town Commercial, Northeast Lucerne, Southeast Lucerne and South Palm Park.

College Park grew mainly in two bursts, 1925 to 1928 and 1945 to 1949. The Northeast and Southeast Lucerne districts sit north and south of Lake and Lucerne Avenues, with the commercial Old Town of about 16 acres between them. South Palm Park covers roughly 60 blocks southeast of Old Town, next to Bryant Park and the Intracoastal Waterway.

The city runs a design review process for historic districts. Ask planning staff whether your address is covered before a buyer plans new windows, fencing or an addition. Platted lots here were deliberately small, since the original lot sales were tied to farmland purchases west of town, so a buyer planning an addition will ask about lot size. Have your survey ready.

  • Confirm the district and any review needed.
  • Keep permits and approvals for past work.
  • Ask about fence rules, which the city publishes in a permit guide.

The city offers its own water and electric service, along with a building division, code enforcement and a business license desk, so several offices may need a call before you close. Natural gas comes through Florida Public Utilities.

Closing your account with city utility customer service is one task. Confirming that no permits or violations are open on the parcel is another, and a buyer's records search will surface them if you do not.

Palm Beach County's tax collector publishes a tax bill explainer. Taxable value is assessed value minus exemptions, multiplied by each taxing authority's millage, and non-ad valorem assessments, such as Solid Waste Authority fees based on property type, are added on top. Ask for a recent bill so you can see which pieces will be prorated.

  • Schedule the utility shutoff or transfer.
  • Ask the building division about open permits.
  • Check code enforcement records.

sections.h2: How Palm Beach County tax bills work for a seller
sections.html:
Each August the county property appraiser mails proposed-tax notices, and by November 1 the tax collector sends out more than 600,000 bills to the addresses the appraiser has on file.

Payment runs November 1 to March 31, and April brings delinquency. For a house you have sold, pass the bill to the new owner or fill in the Property Sold Form. Once a bill is delinquent it cannot be paid online, and a postmark no longer proves timely payment.

The county also offers an installment plan. Enrollment each year runs from November 1 to April 30, and the estimated tax must top $100. Payments are based on the preceding year's tax, due June or July, September, December and March, and a missed first payment drops you from the plan.

sections.h2: What happens to the Save Our Homes cushion when you sell
sections.html:
It stays behind. Closing counts as a change of ownership, which means the buyer starts at full just value on the next January 1.

While you owned the home, the cap limited annual assessment growth to 3 percent or inflation, whichever was lower. The cap was 2.7 percent for 2026 and 2.9 percent for 2025. Portability may carry part of that benefit to a new Florida homestead, within a three-year window and with a March 1 filing.

Ask the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser for your own numbers before signing on a replacement home.

sections.h2: Deed tax and paperwork at a Lake Worth Beach closing
sections.html:
Palm Beach County pays the ordinary documentary stamp rate of 70 cents per $100 of consideration, not the Miami-Dade variation.

The clerk takes the payment when the deed is filed, and the state makes each party to the deed answerable for it. Estate planning transfers have no special exemption. A 2020 advisement concluded that a lady bird deed with the life tenants' full powers retained carried no present beneficial interest and was not taxed on those facts, so take your own deed to an attorney. Deeds need two witnesses.

sections.h2: Behind on the mortgage in Lake Worth Beach
sections.html:
Selling ahead of the auction lets you pay the lender and keep any remaining equity.

After a foreclosure judgment, the clerk holds an auction within a 20 to 35 day window, unless the plaintiff consents to more time. The high bidder deposits 5 percent, and a homestead owner hoping for leftover funds should check with the clerk inside 10 days. A sale of your own before the auction date avoids all of that.

  • Obtain a payoff letter.
  • Calendar every court deadline.
  • Speak with an attorney or a court self-help resource.
  • Compare a cash offer with a short listing.

Once you accept an offer, the title company or closing agent runs the title search, asks the lender for a payoff letter and prepares the deed. Two witnesses sign it, and it is filed with the county clerk, who collects the stamp tax. Property tax for the year is prorated between you and the buyer, and any unpaid balance comes out of your proceeds.

Meanwhile, close your city utility account and hand over permit records, historic district approvals and your survey. A cash buyer can often close faster, yet title and recording steps remain, so ask for the timeline in writing.

faqs.q: How many historic districts does Lake Worth Beach have?
faqs.a: Six: College Park, Old Lucerne, Old Town Commercial, Northeast Lucerne, Southeast Lucerne and South Palm Park. The city's planning staff can confirm your parcel.

faqs.q: What should I do with my tax bill after I sell?
faqs.a: Send it on to the buyer, or complete the tax collector's Property Sold Form. Confirm the proration with your closing agent.

faqs.q: Can I still pay a delinquent bill online?
faqs.a: No. Once a bill is delinquent it cannot be paid online, and a postmark no longer proves timely payment.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed tax in Palm Beach County?
faqs.a: The purchase contract decides, but the state holds both sides liable. The rate is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house I inherited?
faqs.a: Someone with court authority must sign the deed. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is among the deeds the revenue department lists as not taxable. A probate attorney can say whether a shorter summary process applies.
